repo.description:
### Impact

An image processing library bundled with Ghost contained a memory corruption vulnerability (CVE-2026-84383). Because Ghost did not verify the contents of uploaded images, any staff user, including Contributors, could upload a crafted image that reached the vulnerable code. This could crash the Ghost process and may allow code execution on the server.

### Vulnerable versions

This vulnerability is present in Ghost from v6.46.0 up to v6.65.0.

### Patches

v6.67.0 contains a fix for this issue.

### How to update

For self-hosters using Docker, find [Docker's official Ghost image here](https://hub.docker.com/_/ghost). Updating a Docker-based Ghost instance [is documented here](https://docs.ghost.org/install/docker#updating-ghost). 

If your Ghost is a Ghost-CLI install see our documentation on [updating it to the latest version here](https://docs.ghost.org/update). 

### References

We thank [Daniel Lockyer](https://github.com/daniellockyer), [sajdakabir](https://github.com/sajdakabir), Karal, [Anand Prajapati](https://www.linkedin.com/in/anand-prajapati-7a265a369/), and [Vinay Mudunuri](https://github.com/hackncode) for disclosing this vulnerability responsibly.

### For more information

If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, email us at [security@ghost.org](mailto:security@ghost.org).
